comparisons.peer_summary: International sales accounted for 66% of net revenue in 2024 (65% in 2023) and are expected to remain significant; substantially all sales transactions are denominated in U.S. dollars.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and AMD both disclose revenue concentration by geographic region, though AVGO specifically highlights China while AMD provides a broader international mix. AVGO discloses that 20% of net revenue came from shipments to China (including Hong Kong) in fiscal 2024, noting that end customers are often located elsewhere. In contrast, AMD reports that 66% of its net revenue came from international sales in 2024 but does not break out specific country percentages for China in the same detailed manner, nor does it discuss the distinction between shipment location and end-customer location to the same extent.

sentences.text: In fiscal years 2024 and 2023, 20% and 32%, respectively, of our net revenue came from shipments or deliveries to China (including Hong Kong).

As a result, we believe that a substantially smaller percentage of our net revenue is ultimately dependent on sales of either our product or our customers' product incorporating our product, to end customers located in China (including Hong Kong).
International sales as a percentage of net revenue were 66% in 2024 and 65% in 2023.
Substantially all of our sales transactions are denominated in U.S. dollars.

peer_results.rationale: All candidate disclosures for INTC discuss customer concentration (large single customers) or general sales channels/distribution methods. None of the candidates address geographic revenue breakdown, specific dependency on China, or the methodology for assigning geographic revenue vs. end-customer location, which are the core topics of the AVGO disclosure.

comparisons.peer_summary: 2023 was characterized by weak demand in many end markets due to macroeconomic challenges and inventory reductions, leading to significant drops in average selling prices for DRAM and NAND, as well as revenue declines across all segments.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU explicitly disclose regulatory or geopolitical risks related to China impacting their business operations. AVGO discusses the discrepancy between shipment location (China) and actual end-customer dependency. MU discloses that China's Cyberspace Administration conducted a cybersecurity review and determined that Micron products presented a risk, potentially restricting purchases by critical information infrastructure operators in China. Both disclosures highlight China as a specific jurisdiction of regulatory or dependency risk.

sentences.text: As a result, we believe that a substantially smaller percentage of our net revenue is ultimately dependent on sales of either our product or our customers' product incorporating our product, to end customers located in China (including Hong Kong).
The CAC determined that critical information infrastructure operators in China may not purchase Micron products.

comparisons.peer_topic: Geographic revenue designation and international sales mix
comparisons.peer_summary: Revenue by geographic region is based on billing location, which may differ from the end customer's location. Customers outside the United States accounted for 56% and 69% of total revenue in fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and NVDA both disclose methodology for geographic revenue designation and highlight the distinction between billing/shipment location and end-customer location. AVGO discloses that revenue is based on shipment/delivery location specified by partners, noting that end customers are frequently located in countries other than China. Similarly, NVDA discloses that revenue by geographic region is based on billing location, even if attributable to end customers in a different location, and reports 56% of revenue from outside the US. Both companies acknowledge that geographic revenue figures may not perfectly reflect the ultimate end-customer's geographic location.

sentences.text: Although we recognize revenue for the majority of our products when title and control transfer in Penang, Malaysia, we disclose net revenue by country based primarily on the geographic shipment or delivery location specified by our distributors, OEMs, contract manufacturers, channel partners, or software customers.
However, the end customers for either our products or for the end products into which our products are incorporated, are frequently located in countries other than China (including Hong Kong).
Revenue by geographic region is designated based on the billing location even if the revenue may be attributable to end customers, such as enterprises and gamers in a different location.

comparisons.peer_topic: US Export Control Licensing Requirements for China and Other Regions
comparisons.peer_summary: The USG imposed licensing requirements in Q3 FY2023 and July 2023 for A100/H100 exports to China and certain Middle East customers. In Oct 2023, new rules expanded to products exceeding performance thresholds shipped to China and Country Groups D1, D4, and D5 (including Saudi Arabia, UAE, Vietnam), becoming effective in Q4 FY2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVDA disclose specific regulatory constraints and export control impacts related to China. AVGO discusses its dependency on shipments to China and the subsequent distinction between shipment location and end-customer location, implying a risk or adjustment in how revenue is viewed given the geopolitical context. NVDA explicitly details US government licensing requirements imposed on exports to China for specific products (A100, H100, etc.) effective in Q4 FY2024. While AVGO focuses on the revenue recognition nuance and NVDA focuses on export bans, both address the regulatory and operational complexity of selling into China.

sentences.text: In fiscal years 2024 and 2023, 20% and 32%, respectively, of our net revenue came from shipments or deliveries to China (including Hong Kong).

As a result, we believe that a substantially smaller percentage of our net revenue is ultimately dependent on sales of either our product or our customers' product incorporating our product, to end customers located in China (including Hong Kong).

In October 2023, the USG announced new and updated licensing requirements that became effective in our fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024 for exports to China and Country Groups D1, D4, and D5 (including but not limited to Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Vietnam, but excluding Israel) of our products exceeding certain performance thresholds, including A100, A800, H100, H800, L4, L40, L40S and RTX 4090.

The licensing requirements also apply to the export of products exceeding certain performance thresholds to a party headquartered in, or with an ultimate parent headquartered in, Country Group D5, including China.

peer_results.rationale: All candidate disclosures for QCOM discuss revenue sources (IC products vs licensing) and competitive dynamics (vertical integration by customers like Apple). None of the candidates address geographic revenue attribution, China-specific revenue dependency, or the distinction between shipment location and end-customer location.
